attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: The only input is a tinyint; no text input exists. A NULL status is already a fixed case (CASE NULL takes the ELSE branch).

collation-case.notApplicableReason: No text input; the result is a constant chosen by CASE, never compared.

top-ties.notApplicableReason: Scalar function: returns one value, no rows from tables.

identity-gaps.notApplicableReason: Reads no table, no key or sequence.

cases.label: status 6 (second unmapped value above the last WHEN) is the ELSE text
cases.reasoning: A conversion that mapped by range (status > 4) or by array index would agree on 5 but could differ on later values; T-SQL CASE @Status matches only the listed WHEN values.

cases.label: status 127 (signed 1-byte maximum) is the ELSE text
cases.reasoning: tinyint is mapped to smallint on PostgreSQL; a conversion through a signed byte would wrap at 127/128. SQL Server tinyint is unsigned 0..255.

cases.label: status 128 (one above the signed 1-byte maximum) is the ELSE text, not an error
cases.reasoning: 128 overflows a signed byte; SQL Server tinyint accepts it. The PostgreSQL smallint parameter must accept it and fall to ELSE.

cases.label: status 254 (one below the tinyint maximum) is the ELSE text
cases.reasoning: Upper boundary next to 255; a modulo or bit-mask mapping would map 254 to a WHEN text.

cases.label: status 132 (4 + 128, same low bits as 'Complete') is the ELSE text
cases.reasoning: 132 has the same low 7 bits as 4 ('Complete'); a conversion that truncated to 7 bits or a signed byte would return 'Complete'. SQL Server returns the ELSE text.

cases.label: status 1 gives 'Pending' from a varchar literal in an nvarchar(15) result, with no padding
cases.reasoning: The T-SQL WHEN branches are varchar literals ('Pending', no N prefix) assigned to nvarchar(15). A char(15) mapping on PostgreSQL would pad 'Pending' with trailing spaces; SQL Server returns 7 characters.

objections.text: A06 sends status 1 with no tables, exactly the same payload as the hand-derived fixed case for the Pending mapping. That fixed case already checks the unpadded return value and the declared result type.
